scope: read-only source audit; no queue job, model, fit, owner state or frozen packet was modified

production_facing_gap.name: snapshot completion has no atomic admission cutoff
source_counterexample: queue-v3 tick() obtains/releases the shared dispatcher lock and returns a LocalExperimentQueueObservationV1 with all_jobs_recorded=true for the currently admitted plans.
queue-v3 work() tests that snapshot at experiment_queue.py:539–543 and breaks immediately when all_jobs_recorded is true; it then writes a worker receipt with status=finished at lines544–545.

enqueue() independently acquires the same dispatcher lock at lines169–174. After tick() returns and releases the lock but before work() publishes its worker receipt, another cooperating client can enqueue a new valid plan. No store state marks intake closed, and enqueue has no sealed-epoch rejection.

The resulting finished receipt contains the earlier all_jobs_recorded=true snapshot while the store now contains newly admitted pending work. A subsequent status/tick will show it; an orchestrator that treats finished as final can stop and strand it.
production_facing_gap.classification: This is not a false statement that the prior snapshot had completed; it is a missing run-intake lifecycle boundary for callers that need final batch completion or process shutdown. The docs already caution that completion is a current-admissions snapshot and not intake finality. The remaining gap is that no production queue protocol enforces that distinction at the worker boundary.
production_facing_gap.why_lifecycle_successor_does_not_close_i: queue-nonempty-lifecycle-sol-v1/dispatch.py:341–352 defines completion as a current-admissions snapshot; FINDINGS.md:12 and :32 explicitly say new admission reopens work and no intake seal/service protocol exists. Its consumer.py accepts a snapshot only; it is separate research code and is not wired into queue-v3 work()/enqueue().

minimal_correct_approach.continuous_service: Keep an idle-capable supervisor alive after a current snapshot becomes terminal. Report idle_waiting_for_intake (not finished), continue polling/waiting for new admissions, and only stop on an explicit durable shutdown/close operation.
minimal_correct_approach.finite_batch: Add a durable run/epoch row with OPEN/SEALED/FINALIZED state and a monotonic epoch ID. Seal under the same dispatcher lock/SQLite transaction as enqueue. Enqueue must atomically reject admissions to a sealed epoch. Worker may publish finished only after observing SEALED plus zero pending/active/integrity-quarantined work and an explicit nonempty or intentionally empty policy.
minimal_correct_approach.receipt_recovery: Persist the final completion record or its canonical bytes/hash in the same authoritative SQLite transaction as FINALIZED. A filesystem receipt is an idempotent projection: after crash, regenerate/verify the exact same bytes from the sealed epoch. Do not infer finality from an external JSON marker alone.
minimal_correct_approach.next_epoch: A new epoch must be an explicit generation transition with its own admission set and completion receipt; late plans cannot silently reopen/alter the already finalized epoch.
minimal_correct_approach.scientific_boundary: All accepted_execution records remain unqualified. Intake sealing and workflow terminal status must not imply fit success, model promotion, scientific qualification or publication.

crash_and_race_cases_to_test: Enqueue races seal: whichever obtains the shared transaction/lock first decides atomically. If enqueue wins, seal observes the newly admitted plan and cannot finalize; if seal wins, enqueue rejects for that epoch.
Crash before seal commit: intake remains OPEN; restart resumes normally.
Crash after SEALED commit before reconciliation/finalization: restart must reconcile admitted reservations and resume toward the same terminal result; no new admission is allowed in the sealed epoch.
Crash after final DB commit before filesystem receipt: regenerate the identical receipt idempotently.
Crash after receipt publication: replay validates same epoch/receipt and does not create a second finalization or reopen the epoch.
Empty sealed epoch: explicit policy must distinguish no work from completed nonempty work; never use vacuous all-terminal=true as accepted execution.
limits_and_nonclaims: This is a source-interleaving finding; no runtime reproduction or workload benchmark was run.
Does not establish SQLite power-loss durability, backup/restore, portable recovery, intake policy, or thousands-cycle throughput.
queue-nonempty-lifecycle-sol-v1 itself explicitly says it is not production integration, a service shutdown predicate or a thousands-cycle proof.

The separate queue-durable-frontier research prototype documents that direct failed consumers block while grandchildren can wait indefinitely; that is a distinct lifecycle policy gap, not the race analyzed here.
